events.title: Caesar Crosses the Rubicon
events.description: According to the traditional date, Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon River in northern Italy, defying the Roman Senate's order to disband his legions. His act of entering Italy with troops triggered a civil war against Pompey and the Senate's forces.
events.significance: The crossing, often summed up by the phrase 'the die is cast,' led to the fall of the Roman Republic and Caesar's rise to power, paving the way for the Roman Empire.

events.title: World's First Underground Railway Opens in London
events.description: The Metropolitan Railway opened between Paddington (Bishop's Road) and Farringdon Street, becoming the world's first underground passenger railway. It carried tens of thousands of passengers on its first day using steam locomotives.
events.significance: It pioneered urban rapid transit and became the foundation of the London Underground, inspiring subway systems in cities worldwide.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles Takes Effect and the League of Nations Is Established
events.description: The Treaty of Versailles came into force after ratification, formally ending the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers, and the League of Nations came into official existence.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped post-World War I Europe and the League was the first major international organization aimed at maintaining world peace, a precursor to the United Nations.

events.title: First General Assembly of the United Nations Convenes
events.description: The first session of the United Nations General Assembly opened at Methodist Central Hall in London, with delegates from 51 nations attending.
events.significance: It marked the beginning of the UN's operations as the central forum for international cooperation after World War II.

events.title: Spindletop Gusher Launches the Texas Oil Boom
events.description: The Lucas Gusher at Spindletop near Beaumont, Texas, struck oil and blew in at a rate of roughly 100,000 barrels per day, far above any previous U.S. well.
events.significance: The discovery began the modern petroleum industry in Texas, and helped make the United States a leading oil producer and spurred the rise of major oil companies.
